slides.title: Virtual AI Receptionist — Bukowy Dwór & Thermal SPA
slides.subtitle: Client case study: enterprise deployment of ElevenLabs Conversational AI in a spa hotel and health resort, 2026
slides.notes: Open with the business context: the resort, its senior guests and the commercial stakes, before any architecture.

slides.title: Senior Guests Wait. Front Desk Can't Keep Up.
bullets: Health resorts and thermal SPAs: 60–70% of guests are seniors (60+), with a strong preference for telephone calls over apps
Peak inbound waves at 8:00–10:00 AM and 4:00–6:00 PM create call queues, dropped calls and guest frustration
Unanswered call = lost high-margin revenue ($30–$80 per spa treatment, $100–$250 per night)
Human receptionist: ~$25/hr, available 8 hours per shift, with no capacity for proactive pre-arrival calls
slides.notes: Frame the problem from both the guest's perspective and the hotel's P&L before proposing any technical solution.

slides.title: Who Is Calling? Mrs. Sophia, 72 Years Old.
bullets: Speaks slowly and pauses mid-sentence to gather her thoughts
Does not remember medical names: asks for "that spine treatment with warm mud"
Low tolerance for error: hangs up immediately if interrupted or rushed
Asks for an SMS confirmation sent to her own phone or to her daughter's phone
Every architectural decision follows directly from this persona
A design persona representing the typical thermal spa guest, not a generic user
slides.notes: Every latency parameter, voice choice and silence timeout is set around this guest's speech patterns and needs.

slides.title: Meet Anna — Always Empathetic, 24/7
bullets: Powered by ElevenLabs Conversational AI: a unified cloud loop (STT, orchestrator and TTS)
Sub-500 ms real-time latency · warm, measured cadence · 24/7 availability
Omnichannel: handles both telephone (PBX) calls and the interactive web and mobile widget
slides.notes: Explain what the agent is and why it is built this way before the live demonstration.

slides.title: 3 Core Architectural Decisions & Trade-Offs

bullets.text: Native ElevenLabs agent vs. cascaded pipeline: traditional STT → LLM → TTS cascades exceed 2.0 s latency. The native loop achieves ~430 ms. For seniors, latency equals trust.
TTS: Eleven v3 Conversational (not Flash): Flash is fast (75 ms) but sounds mechanical; v3 (~280 ms) delivers warmth and natural intonation.
Acoustic tuning: turn_timeout 3.0 s, speed 0.85x, Patient mode. Accommodates mid-sentence pauses without cutting the guest off.

slides.notes: Each choice was a deliberate trade-off between benchmark speed and conversion for this group of guests.

slides.title: Knowledge Base (RAG): Zero Hallucination Policy
bullets_left: 5 curated Markdown knowledge base files (access, treatments, rooms, dining, policies)
Prompt mode (constant context): standard pricing, cancellation rules, emergency policies
Auto mode (semantic retrieval): detailed treatment descriptions and dietary information
Scales to hundreds of documents without changes to the agent code
bullets_right: Strict grounding: missing information triggers an immediate warm transfer to the front desk. The agent never guesses.
Mandatory balneological safety check: screens for cardiac and acute contraindications before a treatment is booked
An incorrect price is a commercial problem; incorrect medical information is a legal liability
slides.notes: Highlight safety and compliance. In medical wellness, an agent that invents answers is worse than no agent.

slides.title: Anna Doesn't Just Chat — She Executes Actions

rows: Checks available treatment slots in real time
Books the appointment and generates a confirmation code
Validates room inventory and calculates the total stay price
Sends an SMS or Telegram summary with the booking ID
Transfers the call to the front desk or the nursing duty desk

slides.notes: Explain how deterministic tool calls connect the agent to existing hospitality systems (PMS, CRM, telephony). The transfer to a person uses the native ElevenLabs SIP transfer; in the proof of concept it is simulated through a mock webhook.

slides.title: Live Demonstration: 3 Key Interaction Flows
bullets: A. Spa treatment booking with automated SMS summary (happy path)
B. Knowledge base enquiries (RAG, strictly grounded in hotel policies)
C. Medical escalation and live call transfer to the nursing duty desk (safety protocol)
Available live through the website widget and the telephone SIP gateway
slides.notes: Run the live voice demonstration. Keep screenshots of the JSON responses ready in case network latency affects the live call.

slides.title: Two Channels, One Cohesive Voice
bullets_left: Telephone (SIP trunking): 24/7 pickup, 3.0 s silence timeout, paraphrased confirmation
Eleven v3 warm voice, tuned for older listeners
SMS summary sent immediately to the guest or a designated family member
bullets_right: Web and mobile widget: floating button, animated avatar with listening and speaking states
Live streaming transcript and multilingual quick-reply chips (PL, EN, DE, UK, ES)
Booking confirmation card with one-click actions
slides.notes: Emphasise the omnichannel design: the same agent core serves voice calls and website visitors, without duplicated logic.

slides.title: Enterprise Security, Healthcare Data & GDPR
bullets: Zero Retention Mode (ZRM): audio and transcripts are held only in volatile memory, with no disk storage
Conversation history redaction: automatic masking of personal data (national IDs, phone numbers, addresses, health notes)
EU data residency: compute, LLM inference and vector embeddings located within the EU (Frankfurt / Dublin)
Signed URLs with a 15-minute TTL: the web widget connects securely without exposing the API key
slides.notes: For a health resort, data protection and privacy are mandatory requirements, not optional features. A data processing agreement and DPO review are preconditions for go-live.

slides.title: Multi-Tenant Scaling: 1 Agent, 10 Hotels
bullets: The challenge: 10 properties would typically mean 10 separate agents, 10 siloed knowledge bases and linear maintenance cost
The solution: 1 master agent core with dynamic variables (hotel_name, location, reception_phone, pms_id)
SIP UUI (RFC 7433): property context injected into the SIP signalling header for each inbound number
Onboarding a new hotel requires a configuration profile, with no duplication of the prompt
slides.notes: Show that the design scales sub-linearly as properties are added: maintenance does not multiply with each hotel.

slides.title: Cost Efficiency & Return on Investment
bullets_below: The entry plan ($22/mo) costs about the same as one hour of receptionist time (~$25)
The agent operates 24/7/365 with no sick leave and no call abandonment
Return driver: five after-hours bookings per month ($2,000–$4,000 in incremental revenue) would cover the annual contract in under 60 days (planning estimate)
slides.notes: Do not position AI as a headcount reduction. It is a way to capture after-hours revenue that is currently lost.

slides.title: Roadmap: PoC → Phase II → Phase III
bullets: Phase I (MVP, live now): standalone conversational agent, RAG grounding, webhook tool calling, live web widget
Phase II (production pilot): two-way PMS synchronisation (Opera Cloud / Mews), Twilio SIP trunking, multilingual routing (PL / EN / DE)
Phase III (proactive AI): outbound pre-arrival calls, shuttle coordination, medical questionnaire intake, personalised treatment recommendations
slides.notes: Phase III moves the assistant from a reactive call line to a proactive guest-experience service.
